title: This Simple Widget Makes $50K/Month
promo_conflict: The host promotes Starter Story's business-ideas database at the end; no direct promotion by the guest is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: Why do I have to call them? Why do I have to kind of send them an email?
stated_problem.speaker: Tom

idea.name: Avenue website widget
idea.one_liner: A hosted widget for trades and service businesses that lets their customers browse services and book or inquire online; Avenue charges for the software, with pricing and billing cadence not stated.
idea.customer: Trades and service businesses, including electricians and mechanics.
idea.offer: A branded, visual service menu embedded on a client's website, with booking and inquiry flows connected to Google Reservations and the client's website.
idea.revenue_model: Paid software service; price and billing cadence not stated.

key_quotes.quote: Avenue is a website embed, so it goes directly onto the client's website. It just offers all their services in a visual way.
Door to door sales, essentially, like going and showing people our product, initially show it on an iPhone
So that way clients can kind of contact them through Google or they can contact them directly to the website, leading it all to one place, essentially.

claims.claim: The host says an anonymous startup making over $40,000 per month launched about a year earlier.
claims.quote: And an anonymous startup making over $40,000 a month launched just about a year ago.

claims.claim: The host says the app makes over $50,000 per month.
claims.quote: This is Tom, and he built a really simple app that today makes over $50,000 a month.

claims.claim: The host repeats that the app makes over $50,000 per month.
claims.quote: In this episode, we're going to dive into the dead simple app he built that today makes over $50,000 a month.

claims.claim: The host says the growth tactic would help get the first 10 customers.
claims.quote: The growth tactic that almost nobody is using would help him get his first 10 customers, and why he built an app in a category that almost everyone is ignoring.

claims.claim: Tom reports revenue of 85,000 per month in Australian dollars; the transcript renders the currency word as “dolls.”
claims.quote: We do 85,000 a month in revenue now, in Australian dolls, and we built a website widget for trades, and electricians, and mechanics.

claims.claim: Tom describes a Stripe figure rising from “five, 97” in August last year to almost 63,000 Australian now; the opening figure's unit and the period are unclear.
claims.quote: Like I feel like from August last year, five, 97, and then almost now 63,000 Australian.

claims.claim: The host refers to the widget as making $50,000 per month.
claims.quote: Just tell us a little bit about what you were doing before you built this $50,000 per month widget.

claims.claim: The host frames the business as having scaled from an idea to over $50,000 US per month.
claims.quote: Like, how long did it take you from idea to a working project that is now, you know, scale to, you know, over 50,000 dollars US per month?

claims.claim: The host says the business grew from zero to over $50,000 per month.
claims.quote: Can you tell us a little bit more about how you grew this business from zero to over $50,000 a month in a relatively short timeframe, like a year, year and a half.

claims.claim: The host describes the growth period as about a year to a year and a half.
claims.quote: in a relatively short timeframe, like a year, year and a half.

claims.claim: Tom says AWS costs 150; currency and billing period are not stated.
claims.quote: So AWS is 150, which I absolutely love because that's like the essential biggest part of our business is the hosting.

claims.claim: Tom gives figures of 120 for Slack and 130 for Google Workspaces; currency and billing period are not stated.
claims.quote: Slack 120 Google Workspaces 130. That be at 500.

claims.claim: Tom gives a total figure of 500 after listing AWS, Slack and Google Workspaces; currency and billing period are not stated.
claims.quote: Slack 120 Google Workspaces 130. That be at 500.

claims.claim: Tom says Twilio is 4,000 and describes it as a major part of the product's SMS costs; currency and billing period are not stated.
claims.quote: So we do use a lot of like AI voice credits and then Twilio being 4,000, which is a huge part of our SMS course, which is another part of our product.

acquisition_channels.details: Tom describes door-to-door sales, showing the product on an iPhone and later an iPad, with brochures explaining it.
Some businesses referred Avenue to other businesses they thought would benefit.

ideas.delivery: Avenue hosts and maintains the software, embeds it on client websites, and connects booking or inquiries from Google and the website into a central flow.

prices: Google Workspaces: 130 (currency and period not stated)
Combined figure: 500 (currency and period not stated)

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR applies to personal data collected through inquiries and any associated messaging. DMCC Act subscription rules may matter if the service is sold as a consumer subscription; Employment Agencies Regs 2003 are not relevant on the information given.
